history.dynasty: Hoysala (12th century); Vijayanagara; Wodeyars of Mysore
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTED: CSV lists 'Mysore'; the temple stands atop Chamundi Hills, ~13 km from Mysuru city centre. One of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Chamundeshwari, the fierce form of Durga who slew the demon Mahishasura atop the hill - the legend behind Mysuru's name and the state Dasara festival; the goddess is Karnataka's Nada Devi (state goddess) and the tutelary deity of the Mysore maharajas. The original shrine dates to the 12th century (Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana); the tower is attributed to Vijayanagara-era work. The Wodeyars lavishly patronized it: Chamraja Wodeyar IV worshipped here in 1573; Dodda Devaraja Wodeyar built the 1,000-1,008-step stairway in 1659, with the colossal monolithic Nandi at the 700th step and the Mahishasura statue; Krishnaraja Wodeyar III built the seven-tier gopuram (1827 per most sources, 1830 per some - conflict, verify), gifted the Nakshatra Malika jewel (1827) and the Simhavahana (1843). Dravidian and Vesara architecture, east-facing, with silver-plated doors bearing a Ganesha image; one source reports a 15-kg gold idol of the goddess (verify).

name: Chamundeshwari Temple
town_description: Chamundi Hills is a 3,489-ft granite hill on the edge of Mysuru city in Karnataka, named after Goddess Chamundeshwari whose temple crowns its summit. It gives Mysuru its name via the legend of her slaying of Mahishasura, offers panoramic views over the city, and is reached by a 1,000-step stairway (built 1659) or a motorable road with regular buses.

travel.road: Chamundi Hill Road, ~13 km from Mysuru city centre; KSRTC buses run up the hill, or climb the 1,000-step stairway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Dasara (September-October) for the grand festival
